answer: A proposed agent market rejects earning keys without a SHA-256 proof with 30 leading zero bits: each extra alias needs 2^30 expected trials. Verifiers hash the round seed, key and nonce, reject stale proofs and record one permit per key; a proof for one key cannot authorize another. Ten aliases need 10,737,418,240 expected trials. Whether trading saffron or basalt, or selling summit forecasts, keys face the same check. An unpredictable public beacon prevents advance grinding; uniform hashes are assumed, and cheap hardware still favors rich attackers.
